source: Edward Alexander Samuells, Notes on a Forest Race Called Puttooas or Juanga, Inhabiting Certain of the Tributary Mehals of Cuttack, Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal 25(4), printed pp. 295–303
edition_date: The original article and running heads print 1856; the Biodiversity Heritage Library catalog lists the volume's article as 1857. Citation follows the printed 1856 date and records this catalog discrepancy.
scope: Complete article lexical scope pp.295–303; all31 glossary prompts plus2 prose attestations. Source-scope report accounts controls and context across every page and illustration.
alternates: Da or Dagé for water, and Khemé chélo or Juangurrakee for woman. Each pair has source-local variant-qualified keys and an explicit second-to-first variant link.
holds: Zero. All eleven earlier shape-based exclusions are recovered as whole attested responses, with no inferred stems.
rights: Public-domain printed1856 original. BHL marks volume25 public domain. Original page images remain local review cache; the package preserves lexical transcription, attributed short evidence excerpts, source commentary and hashed locators.
provenance: Samuells states on printed p. 301 that he collected the words and phrases himself. He first met Puttooas/Juang in Dhekenal in 1854, saw another group in Hindole in 1855, and visited a village near Bhapore weeks before writing in 1856. He does not assign individual glossary items to those visits or to speakers, so the source-qualified Juang lect has blank coordinates and only this broad historical locality note.
comparison_source: Dalton 1866, Appendix F pp. 266–267, has a Putoons/Juang column, but its underlying collector is unclear. Dalton cites Samuells 1856 for ethnography; the two printed vocabularies are materially nonidentical (for example, Samuells man Moolusso vs. Dalton juang, woman Khemé chélo or Juangurrakee vs. Dalton mukha). Dalton remains analysis-only and is not used as a second independent witness here. The Dalton public-domain scan is https://www.loc.gov/item/tmp92008019/ (local cache SHA-256 17a81c5ad648497061aa6067abe9e1eb866df30934af225e8f13ae52e2178717).
transcription: Exact literal source forms in raw Form and parser Original. Display lowercases only, retaining accents and doubles without phonological assumptions. All whole multiword/inflected responses preserved. Woman Juangurrakee confirmed from960px original.
overlap: All35 literal proposals compared case-insensitively with2,204 other canonical Juang manual rows. One exact match: Minna versus Pinnow1959 minna. Retain both attributed records; spelling agreement alone does not prove independent elicitation or textual dependence.
audit: Complete33-unit/35-form independent review passed with zero errors; independent-full-output-review-20260926.json pins installed CSV/audit/profile. Historical pilot audit preserved.
inapplicable: No native script or separate phonemic transcription. No inferred donor/cognate/derivation links. Dictionary sense numbering is inapplicable.
